meta_title: Distribution Workflow Software for Order Handoffs | VOS
meta_desc: One path from the customer's order to your delivery, the same on every shift. VOS is the distribution workflow software for the first leg of that path.
text: the same path, whether or not anyone is in
less handling on each order that takes it
to put one shared path in place for most distributors
There is a process. It lives in four people's heads.
Ask two staff how an order gets from a chef to the pick list and you get two answers. That is not a documentation problem, it is a path problem:
One takes it on a pad, one texts it to the warehouse, one remembers to enter it. Same business, three paths.
Which items they get, what price, who to call about a short. When Dave is off, the account gets guesswork.
The order was taken and never entered, or entered twice. Nobody can tell you where it stopped, because nothing recorded the handoff.
What distribution workflow software has to pin down
The customer takes the first step, not your staff.

Today the path begins when somebody of yours answers a phone, which means it begins differently every time. Move that start to the buyer and it is identical each time: their guide, their words, their approval.
Begins with whoever knows what is needed
Items and prices come from the guide set up for them
No dependency on who is on shift
Distribution workflow management software, without the build.

You do not need a rules engine to fix this. Orders leave the app by one route you agree with us and land identically each time, which is most of what people want from distribution workflow software in the first place.
One delivery method, agreed with you up front
A file by email, a QuickBooks entry, EDI or a live connection
With a direct feed nobody has to key it in
Nothing for your team to remember to forward
You can tell where an order got to.

Anything out of the app has a reference, a stamped time and the account attached, so "did that come in?" has an answer. Any distribution workflow solution worth running has to make the handoff visible, and that is the piece a telephone call never provides.
A reference number on anything sent from the app
The buyer gets a confirmation when it lands
Kept by account on one screen
Phone orders stay invisible to this, as they always were
A short is a conversation. Have it earlier.
Nothing automates away a line you cannot fill. What changes is the timing: with stock visibility moving alongside the ordering, your people are looking at it while there is still a morning to act in.
Stock across the catalog, moving as your levels do
Orders in earlier, so substitutions are not last minute
A person decides the swap, every time
Sits next to the stock tools you run now
Things that keep the path clean.
Small by themselves, and the reason the process does not drift back.
What an account buys and at what price lives in its guide, not in one colleague's memory of a conversation.
They read the lines and send them. There is no internal sign-off step to chase on your side.
A Day Off Is Not A Crisis
With the path outside your staffing, somebody being off does not change how an account's order arrives.
Draw your order path with us in 20 minutes
Tell us how it runs today and we will point at the legs this would replace.
Agreeing the path takes one conversation
There is nothing to diagram and no process to write up. You tell us two things, we do the rest.
A guide per customer: items, your prices, your codes. However it is held today usually works.
The same destination for every account: an inbox, QuickBooks, EDI or the API. That decision is the whole workflow design.
We set each account up and off it goes
For most distributors the whole thing takes 24 to 48 hours. Buyers get the app and usually order the same day.

Distribution workflow software can mean a modeling platform, or it can mean one dependable path. If you want to model the whole business, you want the middle column. If you want orders turning up in one predictable shape, read ours.
Order starts the same way each time
A single way in to your systems
Handoff leaves a reference and a time
Works when a key person is away
Internal approval chains and task queues
Covers warehouse, delivery and billing steps
Needs somebody to own and maintain it
What people ask about the process
Is VOS distribution workflow software in the usual sense?

Not in the sense of a tool you design processes in. There is no canvas, no rules engine, no task queue and no approval chain here. What VOS does is make one leg of the path fixed: how a customer's order is created and how it reaches you. Everything downstream stays yours to run.
Can we build different paths for different accounts?

The guide is per account, so what a customer can order and at what price varies. Where a completed order goes is agreed with us up front, so it lands the same way whoever is on shift. Fewer variations is the point, and it is why this needs no maintenance.
Who handles it when an item is out?

A person on your team, as now. VOS does not decide substitutions or notify anybody on your behalf. The difference is that orders tend to arrive earlier and stock levels are visible beside them, so the decision happens before picking rather than during it.
Do we need to write the process down first?

No, and that is much of the appeal. Adopting distribution workflow software normally starts with weeks of mapping. Here you decide two things, the guides and the delivery method, and the path follows from those.
How does this work while half our accounts still phone?

You will be running two paths for a while, and it is better to admit that than pretend otherwise. Calls get written up as they are now, with no reference or send time attached. The app path grows as accounts move across.
Does it connect to the systems we already use?

Yes, by whichever single route suits you: by email as a PDF, Excel or Word file, through EDI, into QuickBooks, or straight into your ERP over the API. Take one of the direct feeds and there is no entry step at all.
Will our staff have to work differently?
They work in the same systems they do now. What changes is what turns up in them: finished, coded orders in place of messages to interpret. Nobody has to learn a new screen on your side of the path.
What size of distributor is this aimed at?

Smaller food distributors, independents and DSD rounds included. You need no IT staff, nobody to own the process and no enterprise contract, and we quote per distributor rather than publishing a price list.

hero.lead: VOS builds you no flowchart. It settles the first leg instead. The restaurants on your books talk their order into the app, and it reaches your team by one agreed route, in one shape, whoever happens to be working.
